description: A guide to the hill stations of Maharashtra: Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani, Lonavala and Khandala, car-free Matheran, Bhandardara and Igatpuri, Malshej Ghat, Amboli in the south and Chikhaldara in Vidarbha, with how they compare, the monsoon season, getting there from Mumbai and Pune, and nearby forts and caves.
dek: Maharashtra's hill stations are the Sahyadri escapes of Mumbai and Pune: forts, caves, viewpoints and, in the monsoon, waterfalls everywhere.

intro: Maharashtra's hill stations sit along the Sahyadri, the northern Western Ghats, within a few hours of Mumbai and Pune. Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani are the classic pair, known for viewpoints and strawberries; Lonavala and Khandala are on the Mumbai-Pune expressway; Matheran is closed to private vehicles. Bhandardara, Igatpuri, Malshej Ghat and Amboli are quieter, especially lovely in the monsoon.
Chikhaldara, in Vidarbha near the Melghat Tiger Reserve, is the state's only hill station outside the Sahyadri.
quickAnswer: The main hill stations of Maharashtra are Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani, Lonavala and Khandala, Matheran, Bhandardara and Igatpuri, Malshej Ghat, Amboli and Chikhaldara. The monsoon (June to September) is the most popular season for greenery and waterfalls, and October to February for clear views. Most are two to six hours from Mumbai or Pune by road.
takeaways: Lonavala and Matheran are the easiest trips from Mumbai and Pune.
Matheran bans private vehicles; you walk, ride or take the toy train in.
Mahabaleshwar is busiest in summer and on long weekends; strawberry season is roughly December to March.
The monsoon brings waterfalls but also very heavy rain and crowds at popular spots.
Many forts and caves sit close to these hill stations.

sections.heading: Forts and caves nearby
paras: The Sahyadri hill stations sit among the Maratha forts. Pratapgad is close to Mahabaleshwar, Lohagad and Visapur to Lonavala, and Raigad is a day away. The Buddhist rock-cut caves at Karla and Bhaja are near Lonavala.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Lonavala and Mahabaleshwar have the widest choice, from resorts to villas; weekends and the monsoon are busy, so book early. In Matheran, stays are reached on foot or by horse or hand-pulled rickshaw from the Dasturi entry point, so pack light. Bhandardara and Amboli have simpler resorts and state tourism properties.

sections.heading: Getting there
paras: Lonavala and Khandala are on the Mumbai-Pune expressway and the railway line. Matheran is reached by road to Dasturi or by the toy train from Neral when it runs. Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani are reached by road via Wai, about three hours from Pune. Bhandardara and Igatpuri are near Nashik and the Mumbai-Nashik highway. Weekend traffic on the expressway and ghats can double journey times.

sections.heading: A little history
paras: Mahabaleshwar was developed as the summer capital of the Bombay Presidency from the 1820s, and Matheran was opened up in the 1850s, with its narrow-gauge railway following in 1907. Panchgani grew as a boarding-school town. Much older are the Buddhist caves of Karla and Bhaja and the forts of the Sahyadri, many linked with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

sections.heading: When to go
list: June to September: the monsoon; green, misty and full of waterfalls, but very wet and crowded at weekends.
October to February: clear views and pleasant days; strawberry season in Mahabaleshwar from about December.
March to May: warmer; Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani are popular summer escapes.
Late May to early June: fireflies near Bhandardara, before the rains.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
packing: Rain jacket and umbrella in the monsoon
Shoes with grip for wet laterite
Torch for evening walks in Matheran

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in Maharashtra?
faqs.a: Mahabaleshwar and Lonavala are the most popular; Matheran is the most distinctive.

faqs.q: Which hill station is closest to Mumbai?
faqs.a: Matheran and Lonavala, about two to two and a half hours by road.

faqs.q: Is Mahabaleshwar good in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It is very wet from July to September; many visitors prefer Lonavala or Bhandardara in the rains.
No; vehicles stop at Dasturi, and you continue on foot, by horse or rickshaw, or by the toy train when it runs.

faqs.q: Which is the only hill station in Vidarbha?
faqs.a: Chikhaldara, near the Melghat Tiger Reserve.
